items.title: Snow Brings Austria to a Standstill
items.gist: The season’s first heavy snowfall disrupted travel across much of Austria. The A21 closed, and flights and trains also faced delays.
items.summary: Heavy snow hit many parts of Austria on Thursday, especially in the east. Several vehicles became stuck on roads, and the A21 motorway was closed in both directions. Vienna also saw traffic jams and delays on a suburban rail line. Some flights from Vienna were delayed. Emergency services and road crews worked to manage the disruption.
items.host_open: The snow turned familiar routes into slow journeys today. How did that look from where you are?

items.title: Austrian Teenager Faces Terror Charges
items.gist: Prosecutors have charged a 15-year-old in Innsbruck over an alleged plan involving a teenager in Sweden. The case now moves to court, but the charge is not a conviction.
items.summary: Prosecutors in Innsbruck have charged a 15-year-old with terrorism-related offences. They allege he encouraged a 14-year-old in Sweden to attack people with a knife and gave him advice online. The two teenagers are said to have met through an online forum. The Austrian teenager admitted sending messages, but said he did not understand their seriousness. The charge is not final, no trial date has been set, and he is presumed innocent.
items.host_open: This is a serious case involving very young people and an allegation, not a verdict. How does the legal process look from Austria?

items.title: Austrians Donate More Despite Rising Costs
items.gist: People in Austria gave €1.08 billion to good causes in 2025. Yet higher costs mean charities say each euro may achieve less.
items.summary: A new Austrian fundraising report says donations reached €1.08 billion in 2025. That was about one percent more than in 2024. The report says fewer donors are giving larger amounts. Many people who do not donate say rising living costs make it difficult. Charity groups also warn that higher costs reduce what their funds can achieve. Most charitable funding still comes from private individuals.
items.host_open: People are giving more money overall, even as budgets feel tight. Did that surprise you?

items.title: Russia Threatens Ukraine’s Energy System
items.gist: Ukraine’s president says Russia is preparing a major attack on energy and other infrastructure. The warning comes as winter puts added pressure on the country’s power system.
items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said intelligence reports point to preparations for a major Russian strike. He said energy facilities, logistics and essential services could be targets. Russia has repeatedly attacked Ukraine’s power network during the war. A US envoy described Russian President Vladimir Putin as showing restraint, referring to his agreement not to use nuclear weapons. Ukraine’s government has urged people and services to prepare for possible attacks. The warning is a statement by Ukraine and does not confirm that an attack is imminent.
items.host_open: For people facing another winter under attack, the warning is deeply worrying. How does it look from Austria?

items.title: Israeli Strikes Kill People in Gaza
items.gist: Israeli strikes killed people in Gaza, according to local reports. Israel said one target was a Hamas official; the claims could not be independently verified by AP.
items.summary: Israeli strikes hit Gaza overnight, and local sources reported that ten people were killed. Israel’s leaders said the military killed Khaled Abu Nada, whom they described as responsible for economic and education affairs for Hamas. The Associated Press said it could not independently verify Israel’s claim. The strikes come despite a ceasefire agreement reached more than a year ago. Near-daily Israeli fire and airstrikes have continued, according to AP. The deaths add to the human cost of a conflict with sharply different accounts from the sides.
items.host_open: Reports of more deaths in Gaza are painful to hear. How are you feeling about the news?

items.title: Protesters Challenge Baghdad’s Kurdish Policy
items.gist: Thousands gathered in Irbil to oppose Baghdad’s plans for oil operations and border crossings. The dispute touches on power, resources and the Kurdish region’s autonomy.
items.summary: Thousands of people protested in Irbil, the capital of Iraq’s semiautonomous Kurdish region. They opposed moves by the federal government in Baghdad to take control of oil operations and border crossings. Kurdish authorities have previously managed these areas. The dispute reflects a long-running conflict over political authority and resources. Iraq’s constitution has not resolved all questions about disputed territories. The protest shows that the disagreement remains politically sensitive.
items.host_open: The protest reflects a deep dispute about power and resources. What stands out to you about it?

items.title: EU Leaders Wrestle Over Ukraine Funding
items.gist: EU leaders met to discuss Ukraine’s 2027 financing and the bloc’s next long-term budget. Countries disagree on how much to spend and how to share the cost.
items.summary: European Union leaders gathered in Brussels for a special summit on the next long-term budget. They also discussed how to help finance Ukraine in 2027. The proposed EU budget covers the years 2028 to 2034 and is worth nearly €1.6 trillion. Governments disagree about spending priorities and how to fund support for Ukraine. Russia’s government says EU funding could make Ukraine less willing to seek peace. No final agreement was reported at the start of the talks.
items.host_open: EU leaders have a difficult bill to divide and several priorities to balance. What do you think matters most?

items.title: Spain’s De Cos Picked for ECB Role
items.gist: EU leaders chose Spain’s former central-bank chief to succeed Christine Lagarde at the European Central Bank. His appointment comes as Europe faces inflation and high borrowing costs.
items.summary: European Union leaders chose Pablo Hernández de Cos as the next president of the European Central Bank. He previously led Spain’s central bank and now heads the Bank for International Settlements. He is set to take over from Christine Lagarde, who plans to leave early. The ECB helps set interest rates for countries that use the euro. Leaders are facing inflation linked in part to the war in Iran, as well as concern about government debt. The choice still needs to pass the formal appointment process.
items.host_open: A new central-bank chief will soon face some tough choices on prices and borrowing. Did the selection surprise you?
